Your clipboard flows quietly between phone and PC.
Everything copied on either end gathers here; tap any entry to copy it on this device again.
Every segment of the flow is shown honestly. The PC pairing entrance is here — “Pair now” in the network segment.
Pause sync, private mode, retention — every switch truly works and lands on disk immediately.

Android restricts background clipboard reading, and ClipSync does not pretend otherwise: it uploads automatically while in the foreground; background reading requires completing one route of your choice on the Conduit page. Every capability is judged by live testing — if something cannot be done, it says so.
The pairing entrance stays in the network segment of the Conduit page — you can always find it after this tutorial.
While pairing, both ends show a certificate fingerprint; confirm only when they match — this step prevents pairing with the wrong PC.
Once paired, the network segment is connected and the sync service starts automatically.

The clipboard can always be read while the app is in the foreground; background reading takes a one-time setup on a route of your choice — the highest quality, “Privileged direct read”, is recommended.
No USB cable at hand? Enable Developer options → Wireless debugging, and the PC can run the same one-click start over Wi-Fi.
Each permission is requested only at the moment it is needed; here is what each one is for. Deny any of them and foreground copying and history still work.
Show sync status and “content received” alerts; they never contain clipboard content.
Needed only by the overlay-based background-read routes; skip those routes and it is never asked for.
Exempting the app keeps background sync steadier; without it everything still works, the service is just reclaimed more easily.
Pair with your PC first; the read-route guide lives on the Conduit page and every switch in Preferences — you can come back anytime.
